codes.label: Thread cutting pass
codes.description: Cuts one straight or tapered threading pass to the end point in the block. F is the thread lead per revolution, not a feed rate, so scaling the feed would change the thread. G-code system A spells this G32.

codes.label: Scaling cancel (G-code system B)
codes.description: In G-code system B this code ends scaling, and G92 sets the coordinate system and the top spindle speed. gEdit still reads an S word in such a block as a speed limit, because a program posted for system A writes its clamp as G50 S and is opened with a system-B machine often enough: raising the clamp of a constant-surface-speed program is what lets the spindle run away as the diameter falls.

codes.label: Turning pass
codes.description: Cuts one outside or inside turning pass, straight or tapered, and returns to the start point. It belongs to the motion group, so the next G00 or G01 ends it. G-code system A spells this G90.

params.label: End of the pass along Z
Taper: the difference in radius between the start and the end

codes.label: Threading pass as a cycle
codes.description: Cuts one threading pass, straight or tapered, and returns to the start point, so a thread is written as a list of X values. F is the thread lead per revolution, not a feed rate. G-code system A spells this G92.

params.label: Taper: the difference in radius between the start and the end

codes.label: Facing pass
codes.description: Cuts one facing pass, square or tapered, and returns to the start point. It belongs to the motion group, so the next G00 or G01 ends it. G-code system A spells this G94.

params.label: End of the pass along Z
Taper: the difference along Z between the start and the end

codes.label: Absolute positions
codes.description: Position words are read as coordinates in the active work offset. G-code systems B and C number the distance modes the way a mill does; in system A the same number is a turning cycle and incremental moves are written with U and W.

codes.label: Incremental positions
codes.description: Position words are read as distances from the current position. G-code system A has no G91 and uses U and W for that.

codes.label: Coordinate set, top spindle speed
codes.description: Sets the coordinate system without moving. With an S word it gives the highest spindle speed the control may use for constant surface speed; write it in a block of its own in front of G96. G-code system A uses G50 for this and reads G92 as the single-pass threading cycle, whose F is the thread lead — so gEdit will not scale the F of such a block here either: a program posted for system A and opened with a system-B machine would otherwise have its thread leads multiplied in silence.

codes.label: Work coordinate system preset
codes.description: Puts the work coordinate system back where its work offset says, after a manual move or a shift has displaced it. The block names the axes to reset, each with 0; an axis it does not name keeps its coordinates. This is the G-code system B spelling; system A writes G50.3.

codes.label: Feed per minute
codes.description: F is read as distance per minute. G-code systems B and C number the feed modes the way a mill does; in system A the same number is a facing cycle and the feed modes are G98 and G99.

codes.label: Feed per revolution
codes.description: F is read as distance per spindle revolution, which keeps the chip thickness steady while constant surface speed changes the spindle speed. In G-code system A this mode is G99.

codes.label: Cycle return to the initial level
codes.description: After each hole a drilling cycle pulls back to the level the tool was at when the cycle started, which clears anything in the way. In G-code system A the same number means feed per minute instead.

codes.label: Cycle return to the retract plane
codes.description: After each hole a drilling cycle pulls back only to the R plane, which is quicker. In G-code system A the same number means feed per revolution instead.

templates.label: Program start
templates.description: G-code system B: tape mark, program number, a safe-start line (units, no nose radius compensation, feed per revolution with G95), both axes to the reference point and back to absolute positions (G90).

params.label: Program number
params.help: The number after O, written with at least four digits. O0 is not allowed.

templates.label: Tool start
templates.description: G-code system B: the speed limit (G92 S), the turret station with its offset and a comment, constant cutting speed with the spindle direction, the approach and coolant.

params.label: Highest spindle speed (rpm)
params.help: The speed limit for constant cutting speed; the spindle never turns faster.

params.label: Cutting speed (m/min)
params.help: Constant cutting speed: the control changes the spindle speed with the diameter.
